Title: Passing Values Inside Href Attributes to Laravel Controller - A Comprehensive Guide Introduction Passing values inside the href attribute of HTML links allows you to provide additional context when navigating through different routes in your Laravel application. In this article, we will explore how to pass values from view files to controller methods using the HTTP GET method and redirect back to the same URL with the added parameters. Let's start by learning about routing and the concept of passing data between them. 1. Routing Basics in Laravel Routing allows you to map human-readable URLs to controller actions, meaning that you can easily map specific routes for different user actions like listing or updating data. A simple route definition looks like this: 
Route::get('route-name', 'Controller@MethodName');
In the above example, we are defining a GET request to '/route-name' which will be handled by the 'Controller' class and its 'MethodName' method. You can define different routes for multiple actions within a controller or use route groups to organize similar methods more efficiently. 2. Passing Values in URLs with Parameters Passing values into URLs through parameters is an effective way of keeping the data associated with each action separate from the application logic. When defining your routes, you can assign URL segments directly to a parameter name using ':name' syntax. For example: 
Route::get('switchinfo/{prisw}/{secsw}', 'SwitchinfoController');
This method is perfect for your current case, as it allows you to pass the specific values '$prisw' and '$secsw'. You can then access these parameters in the controller using the following syntax: 
public function Switchinfo($prisw, $secsw) {
    // Your code goes here...
}
3. Passing Values Inside Href Attributes If you need to pass values through your HTML links within the view file, use the following syntax:

{{$info->prisw}} / {{$info->secsw}}

Here, the PHP code in the link tag will generate a valid HTML link with the parameters you provided. The Laravel framework will automatically validate and sanitize these values before passing them to your controller method as per the defined route. 4. Conclusion By following these steps and using proper routing techniques, you can effectively pass values inside the href attributes of your links to the corresponding controller methods in Laravel. Always remember to maintain clear and well-structured code for better application performance, security, and maintenance. For more details on passing data within your Laravel application, visit https://laravelcompany.com/blog/passing-data-in-laravel.
